title: Viniyoga of uttame śikhare

words.gram: stem, quoting the anuvāka’s first word (uttame) by its stem

words.meaning: thus; marks the words before it as a quotation
anuṣṭubh, the metre of four lines of eight syllables

words.gram: compound, n. loc. sg. (M’s spelling of गायत्र्युपस्थाने)
words.meaning: in the upasthāna of the Gāyatrī

words.role: what the mantra is used for

sandhi.rule: a + i becomes e; i before a vowel becomes y

translation.literal: Of the anuvāka “uttame”: Vāmadeva the seer, anuṣṭubh the metre, Gāyatrī the deity, the use in the upasthāna of the Gāyatrī.
translation.readable: Uttame śikhare: seer Vāmadeva, metre anuṣṭubh, deity the Gāyatrī; used when taking leave of her.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: uttame śikhare devī (Mahānārāyaṇa 10.36), with which the Gāyatrī, invited before the japa, is asked to return to her mountain-top. The commas of the witness mark the pauses between the parts; a word before a comma keeps its pausal form.
in_the_rite: Step gayatri-upasthana, before uttame śikhare, in all three services (M only).

flags.text: M writes गायत्र्युपस्थाने for गायत्र्युपस्थाने (gāyatrī + upasthāne). A correction should be considered.
